rows.title: PG&E Announces $13.5 Billion Settlement Of Claims Linked To California Wildfires
rows.standfirst: The utility hopes the settlement will help it emerge from bankruptcy proceedings by the end of the year. When it declared bankruptcy in January, the company faced potential liabilities of $30 billion.

rows.title: Job(-switch) Friday!
rows.standfirst: It's time for our favorite Friday of every month: Jobs Friday! This week, we look at job switching and what it reflects about the tightening labor market.

rows.title: Job Market Surges As Employers Add 266,000 Jobs In November
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers added a better-than-expected number of jobs last month, boosted in part by the return of General Motors workers who had been on strike in October. The unemployment rate fell to 3.5%.

rows.title: How Hard Are Tariffs Hitting The Economy? It Depends On Who You Ask
rows.standfirst: The U.S. economy is still growing, but trade tensions have taken a toll — especially on factories and farms. The trade war's impact on the overall economy is being debated.

rows.title: Uber Received Nearly 6,000 U.S. Sexual Assault Claims In Past 2 Years
rows.standfirst: A new report from Uber, covering 2017 and 2018, says the claims range from unwanted touching and kissing to rape. Also, 19 people were killed in physical assaults during or soon after an Uber ride.

rows.title: UAW Names Rory Gamble As President, The First African American To Lead Union
rows.standfirst: Gamble, 64, will serve the remainder of the term of former head Gary Jones, who has been implicated in a federal embezzlement and bribery scheme at the union and resigned his post last month.

rows.title: Nike Swooshes Out Of Amazon
rows.standfirst: Nike, the country's largest sporting brand, is pulling its products off of Amazon. What spurred this decision, and will other companies follow suit?

rows.title: GM And LG Chem Plan $2.3 Billion Electric Battery Venture In Ohio
rows.standfirst: The two companies expect to create more than 1,100 jobs in northeast Ohio. The new plant will be built near GM's Lordstown facility that was shuttered earlier this year.

rows.title: Why America's 1-Percenters Are Richer Than Europe's
rows.standfirst: The share of total income of the top 1% of earners in the U.S. more than doubled over four decades. But in Europe, the gains were less dramatic. What accounts for the difference across the Atlantic?

rows.title: Russian Hacking Group Evil Corp. Charged By Federal Prosecutors In Alleged Bank Fraud
rows.standfirst: Officials say Evil Corp. developed and distributed a type of malware that infected computers around the world and harvested banking credentials in order to steal some $100 million.

rows.title: Despite Job Boom, More Men Are Giving Up On Work
rows.standfirst: The long economic recovery has brought unemployment to historic lows. But the number of men in the labor force during their prime working age has dropped significantly over the past 50 years.

rows.title: Profiles Of America In Full Employment
rows.standfirst: With the jobless rate at a near 50-year low, employers are struggling to fill open positions. An NPR series looks at the consequences and impacts of an economy at full employment.

rows.title: Delivery Only: The Rise Of Restaurants With No Diners As Apps Take Orders
rows.standfirst: Restaurants without diners are popping up all over the place. "Ghost kitchens" and menus that exist solely in smartphone apps such as DoorDash and Uber Eats seek to feed diners' appetite for delivery.

rows.title: The Case For Hope In 2020
rows.standfirst: Today, the show takes a distinctly positive stance in making the case for being optimistic about the economy in 2020. Five reasons why you should, plus kittens and rainbows.

rows.title: 'The Best Thing You Can Do Is Not Buy More Stuff,' Says 'Secondhand' Expert
rows.standfirst: "Your average thrift store in the United States only sells about one-third of the stuff that ends up on its shelves," Adam Minter says. His book explores what happens to the things that don't sell.

rows.title: Tensions Over Politics At Work? Tell Us About It
rows.standfirst: As the 2020 presidential election heats up, surveys show workplace tensions over politics have increased. Maybe this is true for you. If so, we would love to hear your story.

rows.title: A Trade War Truce?
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration announced it would hit the brakes on a new set of tariffs that were set to go into effect on Dec. 15. Could it be the start of a détente in the ongoing trade war?

rows.title: U.S.-China Trade Deal Phase 1 Is Here; December Tariffs Are Scrapped
rows.standfirst: China says the deal would cover intellectual property protections and currency manipulation, but no details have been released.

rows.title: In Sri Lanka, China's Building Spree Is Raising Questions About Sovereignty
rows.standfirst: A Chinese state-owned operator took control of a port on a 99-year lease after Sri Lanka defaulted on its loans. An adviser to Sri Lanka's president said the government wants China to "give it back."

rows.title: FAA Chief Pushes Back On Boeing Pressure To Return 737 Max Jets To Service
rows.standfirst: A day after hearing criticism from Congress that his agency is too cozy with the manufacturer, the FAA administrator warned Boeing's CEO not to expect quick recertification of the grounded planes.

rows.title: Underrated Trends Of The 2010s
rows.standfirst: The 2010s have been a rich decade for economic megatrends. But some trends haven't gotten the attention they deserve.

rows.title: McDonald's Not Responsible For How Franchisees Treat Workers, U.S. Agency Rules
rows.standfirst: The federal labor law board said McDonald's should not be held liable for labor practices of its franchisees. The ruling directed a judge to approve a settlement in a years-long union case.

rows.title: A Construction Company Embraces Frank Talk About Mental Health To Reduce Suicide
rows.standfirst: The suicide of a construction worker in 2014 became a pivotal event for the Denver-based company that employed him. The death led management to make mental health care a part of the workplace culture.

rows.title: Harvey Weinstein Reaches Tentative $25 Million Deal To Settle Sex Misconduct Claims
rows.standfirst: It isn't clear how many of Weinstein's accusers will agree to the deal. He still faces a criminal trial in New York next month on charges of sexually assaulting two women.

rows.title: YouTube Announces New Anti-Harassment Policy To Fight Racial, Gender, LGBTQ Abuse
rows.standfirst: The Google-owned company has faced scrutiny in the past for failing to protect its users from harassment. It announced new policies Wednesday in an attempt to address the criticism.

rows.title: Federal Workers Poised To Get 12 Weeks Paid Parental Leave
rows.standfirst: The U.S. House of Representatives passed a landmark proposal that would give 2 million workers paid leave upon the birth or adoption of a child, in what worker advocates call a hard-won victory.

rows.title: Debt And The Dairy Farmer
rows.standfirst: Mary Rieckmann and her husband run a small dairy in rural Wisconsin. But a perfect storm of factors has plunged farmers like her into crippling debt.

rows.title: America Will Import More Sugar This Year Than It Has In 4 Decades
rows.standfirst: America's supply of sugar is shrinking because of a poor sugar beet harvest in the northern Midwest. As a result, the U.S. will import more sugar this fiscal year than it has in almost 40 years.

rows.title: The Disappearing Small Farmer
rows.standfirst: It's been a tough year for small farmers hit by trade wars and extreme weather. And as Time's Alana Semuels reports, this latest trouble is just part of a decades-long decline in small-scale farming.

rows.title: Exxon Wins New York Climate Change Fraud Case
rows.standfirst: The state's attorney general argued that the oil giant misled shareholders about the financial risks from climate change.

rows.title: A New Safety Program Takes On Silica Dust Amid A Possible Crisis
rows.standfirst: It will now be easier for the government to inspect shops where workers might get exposed to lung-damaging silica dust. But it's unclear how much it will affect countertop workers.

rows.title: Trump Backtracks On Brazil Steel Tariffs
rows.standfirst: President Trump has reversed himself and decided not to impose tariffs on steel and aluminum imported from Brazil. Financial markets were rattled when he abruptly announced a 25% tax on Dec. 2.

rows.title: WATCH: Carnival Cruises Collide In Attempt To Dock Off Mexico
rows.standfirst: Luckily, the crash in Cozumel looked more serious than it turned out to be. Just a handful of passengers reported minor injuries, and Carnival says the ships remain seaworthy. Still, there's video.

rows.title: Fun Fact Friday!
rows.standfirst: Stacey busts out the funometer and casts judgment on Cardiff's facts.

rows.title: AFL-CIO President Touts Labor's Role In Improving New Trade Deal
rows.standfirst: The comments from Richard Trumka came just before the House overwhelmingly approved the pact called the USMCA.

rows.title: After 2 Years, Trump Tax Cuts Have Failed To Deliver On GOP's Promises
rows.standfirst: The president said it would be "rocket fuel for our economy," but the Republican tax cut passed in 2017 did not pay for itself as promised — nor did it deliver a sustained boost to growth.

rows.title: French Telecom Company Convicted Of 'Moral Harassment' After Employee Suicides
rows.standfirst: The major ruling against Orange, formerly France Télécom, also gave jail time for former CEO Didier Lombard and other executives.

rows.title: In Uncrewed Test, Boeing's Starliner Capsule Fails To Reach Space Station
rows.standfirst: After a flawless launch from Cape Canaveral, Fla., the crew capsule, loaded with 600 pounds of cargo for the station, was unable to reach its intended orbit, Boeing says.

rows.title: We Buy A Junk Bond!
rows.standfirst: Cardiff said the best gift he could imagine getting was a junk bond... so we thought, "Can we actually buy one of those? Also, what exactly is a junk bond?"

rows.title: On Census, Facebook And Instagram To Ban Disinformation And False Ads
rows.standfirst: Under pressure to prepare for 2020 census interference, Facebook says content misrepresenting who can participate and the data the government collects will be banned from its social media platforms.

rows.title: How Online Grocery Delivery Could Help Alleviate Food Deserts
rows.standfirst: Delivery service could make it easier to access fresh, healthy food in these areas, a study finds. It lends support to a pilot program that lets people pay for these groceries with food stamps.

rows.title: How Economics Excludes Black Women
rows.standfirst: Economics is an academic field notorious for its lack of diversity. This is especially true for black female economists. Why are they being left out?

rows.title: Fiat Chrysler And Peugeot Sign 50-50 Merger Deal
rows.standfirst: The combined company will generate nearly €170 billion ($189 billion) annually, which is projected to be the third-most revenue of any automaker — leapfrogging GM, Ford and other companies.

rows.title: Boeing Is So Big That Its 737 Max Production Halt Will Slow The Economy
rows.standfirst: The aircraft giant is the top U.S. exporter, and its decision to suspend production of the 737 Max is likely to ripple through the supply chain. Several analysts project that the move will cut growth.

rows.title: Judge Approves PG&E $24.5 Billion Plan For Wildfire Victims And Insurance Companies
rows.standfirst: The beleaguered utility faces others obstacles such as winning California Gov. Gavin Newsom's approval for its restructuring plan and a bid by hedge funds to gain control of the company.

rows.title: The Great British Bicycle Bubble
rows.standfirst: We continue our series on financial bubbles with the British bicycle mania of the 1890s and the trail of bankrupt companies it left behind.

rows.title: A Decade Marked By Outrage Over Drug Prices
rows.standfirst: Nearly 1 in 4 Americans has trouble affording prescription drugs, according to a Kaiser Family Foundation poll. Over the past decade, high prices of several medicines have become flashpoints.

rows.title: Carlos Ghosn Fled Japan Trial For Lebanon. His Lawyer: 'How Could He Do This To Us?'
rows.standfirst: The former Nissan chairman, who faced up to 15 years in prison over a set of charges over financial misconduct in Japan, was set to stand trial in Japan in April.

rows.title: Immigration Raids, Burger Wars And Other Business Stories You May Have Missed In 2019
rows.standfirst: Engineered meat, immigration raids on chicken plants, and the big target on the backs of big technology companies are some of the business stories that made headlines in 2019.

rows.title: The Roman Financial Crisis Of A.D. 33
rows.standfirst: What lessons should we learn from one of the earliest documented financial crises in history?

rows.title: A Decade After A Fearful Market Hit Bottom, Stock Bulls Continue Historic Run
rows.standfirst: The S&P 500 has seen a nearly fivefold increase since the depths of the Great Recession. But some analysts say the bull market may have gone on too long, encouraging investors to take more risks.

rows.title: Tracing Your Family's Roots May Soon Get A Lot More Expensive
rows.standfirst: Access to some genealogical records kept by the U.S. government may get a lot more expensive, especially for those seeking family records for immigrants from the late 1800s to mid-1900s.

rows.title: Spotify Becomes Latest Tech Company To Hit Pause On Political Ads
rows.standfirst: Starting early 2020, the company says it will no longer sell paid political advertisements for its streaming service. The move follows similar decisions by Twitter and Google.

rows.title: The Work Week, Episode 4: Is The Unemployment Rate Broken?
rows.standfirst: Economist Jared Bernstein thinks it's about time we admit that the unemployment rate is not as useful as it used to be. He offers three alternative indicators.

rows.title: The Work Week, Episode 3: Gender Segregation In The Workplace
rows.standfirst: The most common jobs for men and the most common jobs for women tend to be different — and this separation has big effects for everyone.

rows.title: Would You Lend Your Voice To Our Experiment?
rows.standfirst: NPR is running an experiment in an effort to figure out how accurately voice-to-text algorithms interpret English speakers of all backgrounds.

rows.title: The Work Week, Episode 2: What Happened To U.S. Workers?
rows.standfirst: The share of people aged 25 to 54 in the labor force has fallen in the past couple of decades. What happened?

rows.title: 6-Year-Old Finds Message Alleging Chinese Prison Labor In Box Of Christmas Cards
rows.standfirst: "We are foreign prisoners in Shanghai Qingpu prison China," the note said in English. "Forced to work against our will. Please help us and notify human rights organization."

rows.title: The Work Week, Episode 1: The Strike That Changed U.S. Labor
rows.standfirst: The 1937 union agreement between General Motors and the United Auto Workers union ushered in a period of tremendous worker prosperity and union strength. But today, labor is nowhere near a powerful as it used to be. What happened?

rows.title: Boeing CEO Dennis Muilenburg Is Out
rows.standfirst: Boeing statement: "The Board of Directors decided that a change in leadership was necessary to restore confidence in the Company." More than 300 people have died in Boeing 737 Max plane crashes.

frame: Up to15 visible Business-archive cards at four fixed weekly endpoints, restricted to each block; not a full-publication census
